name: Tía Luz
persona: Warm, nosy, speaks in proverbs. Misses her kitchen and feeds everyone gossip like tortillas. Lately she cannot stop turning over who would steal a dead woman's portrait.
hook: feeds everyone gossip like tortillas; can't keep a secret past supper

name: Bruno el Sepulturero
persona: Gruff, slow to trust, talks to graves more than people. Knows where every story is buried. Someone is blaming him for the missing portrait — he wants the real thief found before the rumor sticks.
hook: counts graves when nervous; trusts stones more than spirits

name: Doña Sefa
persona: Serves aguas frescas and sharp observations. Nothing gets past the counter of La Catrina Feliz. She keeps a tally of who profits from the stolen portrait — envy leaves marks, like wax on a sleeve.
hook: keeps her recipe closer than her rosary

name: Ramón el Trovador
persona: Turns everything he hears into verses — and everything he envies into excuses. Sings La Golondrina's tunes like they're his own; her candle burns brighter every year while his name dims.
hook: versifies everything — a bad secret keeper in perfect meter, and a worse liar when cornered

name: Abuela Inés
persona: Sits by the fountain counting what the water remembers. Sees more than she says. She mourned La Golondrina twice now — once at the funeral, once at the empty frame.
hook: believes the fountain talks back — she's usually right

name: Solorio
persona: Barely there, barely remembered. Answers in half sentences, hopes someone says his name. He thinks he saw someone at the frames at dusk — if he could only hold the memory.
hook: forgot his own name; follows whoever smells of marigold

name: Violeta
persona: Young, wide-eyed, repeats whatever she last heard like it's gospel. Collects petals and stories with equal delight. She heard someone humming La Golondrina's tune by the frames and cannot let it go.
hook: repeats the last thing she heard as if it's gospel — the village's fastest ear

name: Padre Aurelio
persona: Solemn keeper of the candles. Believes remembrance is a duty, not gossip — but he notices everything and forgives slowly. He wants her portrait back on the altar before the vigil ends.
hook: hears confessions and keeps them all — mostly

name: La Viuda Carmen
persona: Quiet, spectral-calm. She leaves candles on graves nobody else visits and can hear the spirits who are fading before anyone else sees it. They whisper that she steals photos — she wants the truth out before the whisper hardens.
hook: leaves marigolds on unmarked graves; whispers to the fading
